"""MB-1880 oversize bore - computed pattern checks. Reads inputs/quality, writes out/figures.csv + out/analysis.json.
Usage: python -I scripts/analyze_mb1880.py <inputs/quality dir> <out dir>"""
import csv, json, sys, statistics as st
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

src, out = Path(sys.argv[1]), Path(sys.argv[2])

def read(name):
    lines = [l for l in (src / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if l and not l.startswith("#")]
    return list(csv.DictReader(lines))

insp = read("inspection_measurements.csv")
maint = read("maintenance_log.csv")
prior = read("prior_ncrs.csv")
for r in insp:
    r["t"] = datetime.fromisoformat(r["timestamp"]); r["x"] = float(r["bore_dia_mm"]); r["seq"] = int(r["part_seq"])
for m in maint:
    m["t"] = datetime.fromisoformat(m["timestamp"])
insp.sort(key=lambda r: r["t"])

LSL, USL = 22.000, 22.021   # MB-1880 rev B sheet 2 note 4
F = []
def fig(name, value, source, query):
    F.append({"figure": name, "value": value, "computed_from": source, "filter_or_query": query})
    return value
um = lambda v: round(v * 1000, 1)

# ---------- time alignment ----------
offsets = sorted({r["timestamp"][-6:] for r in insp} | {m["timestamp"][-6:] for m in maint})
fig("Distinct UTC offsets across inspection + maintenance timestamps", ";".join(offsets), "both CSVs", "timestamp[-6:]")
naive = sum(1 for r in insp if r["t"].tzinfo is None) + sum(1 for m in maint if m["t"].tzinfo is None)
fig("Zone-naive timestamps", naive, "both CSVs", "tzinfo is None")
chg = [m for m in maint if "insert replaced" in m["event"]][0]
first_new = min((r for r in insp if r["tool_id"] == "T7-0032"), key=lambda r: r["t"])
last_old = max((r for r in insp if r["tool_id"] == "T7-0031"), key=lambda r: r["t"])
gap = (first_new["t"] - chg["t"]).total_seconds() / 60
fig("Anchor: maint insert change -> first T7-0032 inspection (min)", round(gap), "maintenance_log r2; inspection r11", "tool_id=='T7-0032' first row vs event 'insert replaced'")
fig("Anchor ordering consistent (last T7-0031 < change < first T7-0032)", last_old["t"] < chg["t"] < first_new["t"], "both CSVs", "timestamp compare")

# ---------- spec check ----------
oos = [r for r in insp if r["x"] > USL or r["x"] < LSL]
fig("Inspection rows", len(insp), "inspection_measurements.csv", "all data rows")
fig("Rows out of spec (>22.021 or <22.000)", len(oos), "inspection_measurements.csv", "bore_dia_mm outside [22.000,22.021]")
fig("Out-of-spec rows: lots", ";".join(sorted({r['lot'] for r in oos})), "inspection_measurements.csv", "lot of OOS rows")
fig("Out-of-spec rows: part_seq", ";".join(str(r['seq']) for r in oos), "inspection_measurements.csv", "part_seq of OOS rows")
fig("Max bore measured (mm)", max(r["x"] for r in insp), "inspection_measurements.csv", "max(bore_dia_mm)")
fig("Max bore excess over USL (um)", um(max(r["x"] for r in insp) - USL), "inspection_measurements.csv", "max - 22.021")

# ---------- SPC: I-MR on T7-0031 points ----------
old = [r for r in insp if r["tool_id"] == "T7-0031"]
xs = [r["x"] for r in old]
mr = [abs(b - a) for a, b in zip(xs, xs[1:])]
cl = st.mean(xs); mrbar = st.mean(mr); sig = mrbar / 1.128
ucl, lcl = cl + 3 * sig, cl - 3 * sig
fig("SPC basis", f"Individuals (I-MR) chart, n={len(xs)} points, lots {','.join(sorted({r['lot'] for r in old}))}, insert T7-0031 only, sigma=MRbar/1.128", "inspection_measurements.csv", "tool_id=='T7-0031'")
fig("SPC centreline (mm)", round(cl, 4), "same computation", "mean(x)")
fig("SPC MR-bar (um)", um(mrbar), "same computation", "mean(|x_i - x_i-1|)")
fig("SPC sigma-hat (um)", um(sig), "same computation", "MRbar/1.128")
fig("SPC UCL (mm)", round(ucl, 4), "same computation", "CL + 3 sigma")
fig("SPC LCL (mm)", round(lcl, 4), "same computation", "CL - 3 sigma")
beyond = [r for r in old if r["x"] > ucl or r["x"] < lcl]
fig("Points beyond control limits", ";".join(f"{r['lot']}#{r['seq']}={r['x']}" for r in beyond) or "none", "same computation", "x>UCL or x<LCL")
if beyond:
    fig("Max point minus UCL (um)", um(max(xs) - ucl), "same computation", "max(x) - UCL")
# Rule: trend - longest run of strictly increasing consecutive points
run = best = 1
for a, b in zip(xs, xs[1:]):
    run = run + 1 if b > a else 1; best = max(best, run)
fig("Run rule checked: trend (>=6 consecutive increasing, Nelson rule 3)", f"longest increasing run = {best} points -> {'FIRED' if best >= 6 else 'not fired'}", "same computation", "consecutive x_i > x_i-1")
# Rule: 9 same side of CL
side = run2 = best2 = 0
for x in xs:
    s = 1 if x > cl else -1 if x < cl else 0
    run2 = run2 + 1 if s == side and s != 0 else 1; side = s; best2 = max(best2, run2)
fig("Run rule checked: 9 on one side of CL (Nelson rule 2)", f"longest same-side run = {best2} -> {'FIRED' if best2 >= 9 else 'not fired'}", "same computation", "sign(x - CL)")
# 2 of 3 beyond 2 sigma same side
z = [(x - cl) / sig for x in xs]
r5 = any(sum(1 for v in z[i:i+3] if v > 2) >= 2 or sum(1 for v in z[i:i+3] if v < -2) >= 2 for i in range(len(z) - 2))
fig("Run rule checked: 2 of 3 beyond 2 sigma (Nelson rule 5)", "FIRED" if r5 else "not fired", "same computation", "z=(x-CL)/sigma")
fig("Note: limits computed on a drifting series", "CL/limits are inflated by the trend itself; the trend rule is the valid signal", "interpretation", "-")

# Drift magnitude and slope vs time
t0 = old[0]["t"]
hrs = [(r["t"] - t0).total_seconds() / 3600 for r in old]
mx, my = st.mean(hrs), cl
slope = sum((h - mx) * (x - my) for h, x in zip(hrs, xs)) / sum((h - mx) ** 2 for h in hrs)
ssr = sum((x - (my + slope * (h - mx))) ** 2 for h, x in zip(hrs, xs)); sst = sum((x - my) ** 2 for x in xs)
fig("Total drift on T7-0031, first to last point (um)", um(xs[-1] - xs[0]), "inspection_measurements.csv", "T7-0031 last x - first x")
fig("Elapsed time on T7-0031 measured span (h)", round(hrs[-1], 1), "inspection_measurements.csv", "last t - first t")
fig("Linear slope bore vs time on T7-0031 (um/h)", round(slope * 1000, 3), "same computation", "OLS x ~ hours")
fig("R^2 bore vs time on T7-0031", round(1 - ssr / sst, 3), "same computation", "1-SSR/SST")
# within-lot slopes per part
for lot in sorted({r["lot"] for r in old}):
    rows = [r for r in old if r["lot"] == lot]
    if len(rows) >= 2:
        a, b = rows[0], rows[-1]
        fig(f"Within-lot wear rate {lot} (um/part)", round((b["x"] - a["x"]) * 1000 / (b["seq"] - a["seq"]), 3), "inspection_measurements.csv", f"lot=={lot}, (x_last-x_first)/(seq_last-seq_first)")
# Extrapolate where L-0411 crosses USL using its own within-lot rate and L-0412 rate
l11 = [r for r in old if r["lot"] == "L-0411"]
rate11 = (l11[-1]["x"] - l11[0]["x"]) / (l11[-1]["seq"] - l11[0]["seq"])
cross11 = l11[-1]["seq"] + (USL - l11[-1]["x"]) / rate11
fig("L-0411 headroom to USL at last measured part #70 (um)", um(USL - l11[-1]["x"]), "inspection_measurements.csv", "22.021 - x(L-0411 #70)")
fig("L-0411 projected USL crossing at its own rate (part_seq)", round(cross11), "same computation", "70 + headroom/rate_L-0411 (linear extrapolation, NOT a measurement)")
l12 = [r for r in old if r["lot"] == "L-0412"]
fig("L-0412 first part (#1) bore vs USL (um over)", um(l12[0]["x"] - USL), "inspection_measurements.csv", "x(L-0412 #1) - 22.021")
# Post-change

# MB-1880 rev B — Oversize Bore A: Root Cause Investigation and Corrective Action Plan

**Status: INTERNAL DRAFT. Not the issued 8D.** The formal 8D and the customer pack are **blocked**: no NCR has been raised from the 2026-11-11 inspection finding, so no NCR `approval_state = approved` exists. The requirement *is* locatable (MB-1880 rev B, sheet 2, note 4), so that is not the blocker. To unblock, raise and approve the NCR via `ncr-writeup`. The investigation below runs as a draft in the meantime.

Prepared 2026-11-15 from SYNTHETIC test data in `inputs/quality/`. Every number below comes from `out/MB-1880_figures_block.csv`, which `scripts/analyze_mb1880.py` produced.

---

## 0. Summary

- **What was found:** Bore A on MB-1880 rev B measured as large as **22.034 mm** against **22.000 +0.021/−0.000** (USL 22.021). That is **13.0 µm over the upper limit**. In-process data puts **3 of 3** sampled L-0412 parts out of spec (part #1, #90, #180). Final inspection found 3 of 5 out (finding.txt).
- **Act today — escape:** 30 parts from lot L-0412 shipped to **Northwind Robotics on 2026-11-11 08:00 (PS-5521)**. That was four days ago and no customer notification is on file. Check the contractual notification clock now. It may already have passed.
- **The scope is larger than the finding:** **at least 300** (all of L-0412), **plus the tail of L-0411 / WO-8101**, whose quantity and location are not in the data (§3).
- **Leading cause (candidate, not concluded):** insert **T7-0031** stayed in the boring head through **4 lots** with **no recorded change**. Bore A grew **26.0 µm** in a monotonic trend (longest increasing run **10 points**; R² vs time **0.876**). Replacing the insert brought the next part back to **22.007** (step **−27.0 µm**). The fault sits with the T7 insert-in-service condition. The data **cannot yet separate** two growth mechanisms: insert-edge degradation (C1) and T7 offset or boring-head setting drift that the insert change reset (C2). One cheap test separates them (§5).
- **This is a recurrence:** NCR-0219 (2026-04-14) had the same part, characteristic and stated cause. **CAPA-071 (change the insert every 600 parts) was never verified effective, and it did not hold.** The SPC trend rule fired at **2026-11-10 07:20**, **7.83 h** before the first out-of-spec part. No reaction plan existed to act on it.
- **Supplier-caused flag: not raised.** No candidate points at purchased material.

---

## 1. Requirement

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Document | MB-1880 drawing rev B, sheet 2 (notes page) | `MB-1880_drawing_revB_notes.md` |
| Locator | Note 4, Bore A | same |
| Characteristic | Diameter, Ra 1.6 | same |
| Stated value | Ø22.000 +0.021/−0.000 mm (22.000–22.021) | same |
| Related note | Note 5: anodize Type II black after machining, bore masked | same. The coating cannot be the cause (it is masked, and anodize would shrink a bore, not enlarge it) |

---

## 2. Problem description (D2 content)

At 2026-11-11 10:05, final inspection (inspector named in finding.txt) measured Bore A at 22.034, 22.031 and 22.029 mm on 3 of 5 sampled parts from **WO-8102 / lot L-0412**. These parts were machined on **VMC-03, 2nd shift, 2026-11-10**. The in-process inspection export agrees: L-0412 #1 = 22.022, #90 = 22.029, #180 = 22.034, all above the 22.021 USL. The out-of-spec rows came from one lot only (L-0412). The defect is a measured dimensional nonconformance, not a subjective one.

`qty_found` is 3 (final-inspection sample of 5) and 3 in-process rows. These may overlap: the export carries no part serials to tell.

---

## 3. Suspect scope and containment (D3 content — feeds the NCR)

### Scope: at least 300, plus an unquantified L-0411 tail

| Lot / WO | Reasoning | Suspect |
|---|---|---|
| **L-0412 / WO-8102** | Every sampled part is out, from part #1 (22.022, 1.0 µm over) to #180. The insert was unchanged through the whole lot. 2 of the 5 final samples were in spec, so the lot needs a 100 % sort, not blanket scrap. | **300** (whole lot) |
| **L-0411 / WO-8101** | The last measured part, #70, read 22.019, only **2.0 µm** below USL. The next measured part on the same insert is L-0412 #1 at 22.022. The drift is monotonic (trend rule fired), so L-0411 parts after #70 lie between 22.019 and 22.022 and may be over the limit. Linear extrapolation at L-0411's own wear rate puts the crossing near **part #139**. That is an estimate, not a measurement. **Lot quantity and location are not in the data.** | **unknown, so suspect from #71 to end of lot** |
| L-0410 / WO-8100 | Bounded by monotonic drift: every L-0410 part was cut before L-0411 #1 (22.017), which is in spec. | Not suspect (bounding assumption: monotonic drift) |
| L-0409 / WO-8099 | Max measured 22.012. Bounded the same way. | Not suspect |
| L-0413 / WO-8103 | New insert T7-0032. First part 22.007. | Not suspect on current data |

`qty_suspect` = **at least 300**. `qty_suspect_is_minimum` = **true**: the L-0411 tail has not been counted or located.

### Containment, by location

| Location | Qty | Checked | Action | Urgency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| At customer: Northwind Robotics (PS-5521, shipped 2026-11-11 08:00) | 30 | Yes, per finding.txt | Notify Northwind and ask them to quarantine the PS-5521 receipt. Offer replacement or sort. **Check the contractual notification clock first. Four days have passed.** | **Immediate** |
| Installed at customer | unknown | **No** | Ask Northwind whether any of the 30 have been assembled | **Immediate** |
| In transit | 0 recorded | **No** | Confirm with shipping whether PS-5521 was delivered. Confirm no other shipment carries L-0412 or the L-0411 tail | Immediate |
| WIP at machine (VMC-03 queue) | 120 | Yes, per finding.txt | Hold-tag NCR. 100 % air-gauge or bore-gauge Bore A. Segregate >22.021 | Same day |
| Finished goods FG-2 rack 14 | 150 | Yes, per finding.txt | Move to quarantine. 100 % measure Bore A | Same day |
| **L-0411 / WO-8101 (all locations)** | unknown | **No** | Find quantity and every location, including shipments, through ERP/shipping. Hold and measure parts after #70. If any have shipped, they are a second possible escape | **Immediate** |

`escape_occurred` = true (30 at Northwind). `escape_detected_at` is no later than 2026-11-11 10:05, when the finding recorded the shipment. The customer notification is `ncr-writeup`'s to draft against the contract clock. **Run it first.**

---

Each link carries its own For and Against lines, with citations. Insp = `inspection_measurements.csv`, Maint = `maintenance_log.csv`, Prior = `prior_ncrs.csv`.

### Shared trunk: confirmed by the data and common to C1 and C2

> **T1. Insert T7-0031 stayed in service across 4 lots, from 2026-11-09 07:10 to 2026-11-10 21:50, with no change**
> **For:** `tool_change_since_last = no` on all 9 T7-0031 rows after the first (Insp r2–r10). Maint has no T7 event until 2026-11-11 06:40.
> **Against:** The inspection export is a sample. An unlogged reset or offset touch between samples cannot be ruled out, but tool_id never changes.
>
> **T2. Bore A grew steadily while T7-0031 stayed in, and returned to nominal when it came out**
> **For:** +26.0 µm from first to last T7-0031 point. Longest increasing run 10 points (Nelson rule 3 fired). R² vs time 0.876. After the insert change, L-0413 #1 = 22.007 (step −27.0 µm), which matches the 22.008 start on T7-0031 (Insp r1, r11; Maint r2).
> **Against:** Only one post-change point exists. One point shows a reset. It does not show sustained capability.

### C1 (tied first): insert-edge degradation on T7-0031 grew the cut diameter

`T7-0031 kept past its useful life (T1)` → **`count exceeded the CAPA-071 600-part limit`** → `edge condition changed (wear, chipping or built-up edge on 6061)` → `bore cut progressively larger` → `oversize from the end of L-0411 / start of L-0412`

| Link | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| **Count exceeded 600 parts** | At 300 per lot, like L-0412, the insert would have cut about 1080 parts. That figure is an **assumption** (figures block). | The only computed lower bound is **390 parts** (sum of the highest sampled part_seq per lot). Lot quantities for WO-8099/8100/8101 are not in the data. **This link has no verified For evidence. It is the weak point of this chain.** |
| Edge condition changed | NCR-0219 named "boring insert wear beyond 900 parts" for the same defect (Prior r1). Built-up edge is a common failure mode in 6061. | Nobody has examined T7-0031. **Plain flank wear on a boring insert normally makes the bore *smaller*, not larger.** To produce oversize, the mechanism has to be BUE, chipping or a geometry change, and none of those is evidenced yet. |
| Bore cut larger | T2 | Same as T2 |
| L-0412 out from part #1 | L-0412 #1 = 22.022, 1.0 µm over. L-0411 #70 headroom was 2.0 µm (Insp r7–r8). | None |

- **Kill:** T7-0031 shows only normal flank wear and no BUE or chipping. Or T7-0031 refitted at the current offset cuts near nominal.

`T7 diameter set by a wear offset or adjustable boring head` → **`offset was incremented, or the head setting crept outward, during the run`** → `bore cut progressively larger` → `insert change at 06:40 on 11-11 reset the setting` → `size returned to 22.007`

|---|---|---|

Ranking C1 ahead on that basis would repeat the earlier conclusion without new evidence.

### C3 (low): Coolant concentration change of 6 % to 8 % (2026-11-08 16:00) accelerated wear or BUE

`coolant change` → `changed edge behaviour or thermal state` → `faster bore growth`

| Link | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| Coolant change | A process change on VMC-03 **15.2 h** before the first measurement (Maint r1) | **0** inspection rows exist before the change, so there is no baseline to compare against (figures block) |
| Changed edge/thermal behaviour | None in data | A higher concentration normally *reduces* BUE in aluminium. **No For evidence. Weak point.** |
| Faster growth | None | Size returned to 22.007 with a new insert and **no coolant reversal recorded** (0 later coolant events). Coolant alone cannot explain the size. At most it changes the wear rate |

- **Confirm:** On insert T7-0032 at 8 %, the bore-growth rate per part clearly exceeds the rate at 6 % concentration, from historical runs.
- **Kill:** The T7-0032 growth rate at 8 % matches the pre-2026-11-08 rate, if any history exists.

### C4 (low, effectively killed): thermal drift, shift effect, or operator practice

`2nd shift / evening thermal state or practice` → `larger bores`

| Link | For | Against |
|---|---|---|
| Shift/operator effect | 3 of 5 shift-2 samples were out of spec. 0 of 6 shift-1 samples were. | Shift and operator are **fully confounded** (shift 1 is OP-11 and shift 2 is OP-23 on every row), so they cannot be separated. # 8D Report — DRAFT-WO-8102-L-0412
*Synthetic test data. This is the internal 8D. There was no controlled 8D template on file, so it uses the standard eight-discipline layout; swap in your template before issue. NCR approved as drafted by Test Quality Owner (LEGION WO-LMFG-004 test operator) on 2026-11-15; no time of day was given.*

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| NCR / site | DRAFT-WO-8102-L-0412 / EPW1 (test) |
| Part | MB-1880 rev B, Bore A, VMC-03, tool T7 |
| Work order / lot | WO-8102 / L-0412, plus the L-0411 tail (WO-8101) |
| Requirement | Drawing rev B, sheet 2, note 4: Ø22.000 +0.021/−0.000 mm |

| Supplier-caused flag | Not raised |

## D1 — Team (proposed)
- **8D owner:** Test Quality Owner.
- **To be assigned:** tooling engineer, VMC-03 cell lead (both shifts), maintenance, Northwind contact.
- **Also on the team:** the inspector who found the problem.

## D2 — Problem
- **What:** Bore A is oversize, up to **22.034 mm** against a **22.021** maximum (**13.0 µm** over).
- **Evidence:** at final inspection, 3 of 5 sampled parts were over. In-process checks on L-0412 found 3 of 3 over: part #1 at 22.022, #90 at 22.029, #180 at 22.034.
- **Where and when:** VMC-03, 2nd shift, 2026-11-10.
- **How many:** at least 300 (all of L-0412), plus the L-0411 parts made after #70. Part #70 measured 22.019, and the next part measured, L-0412 #1, was already 22.022. The quantity and location of those L-0411 parts aren't known.
- **Escape:** 30 parts went to Northwind Robotics on 2026-11-11 at 08:00 (packing slip PS-5521).
- **Not assessed:** surface finish (Ra 1.6) wasn't in the inspection data.

## D3 — Containment

| # | Location | Qty | Checked | Action | Urgency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | At Northwind (PS-5521) | 30 | yes | Notify within the contract deadline, ask them to quarantine, offer sort or replacement. **Four days since shipment.** | Immediate |
| 3.2 | Installed at customer | unknown | **no** | Ask Northwind whether any have been assembled | Immediate |
| 3.3 | In transit | 0 recorded | **no** | Confirm PS-5521 was delivered and that no other shipment carries suspect parts | Immediate |
| 3.4 | Waiting at VMC-03 | 120 | yes | Hold, measure every bore, send any over 22.021 to MRB | Same day |
| 3.5 | Finished goods FG-2 rack 14 | 150 | yes | Quarantine and measure every bore | Same day |
| 3.6 | L-0411 / WO-8101 | unknown | **no** | Find the quantity and every location, including shipments; hold and measure parts made after #70 | Immediate |
| 3.7 | VMC-03 process | — | — | Measure the first part and every 25th part; change the insert at 22.015 or at every new lot | Immediate |
| 3.8 | Insert T7-0031 | 1 | — | Quarantine it and keep it; it is the evidence for the test below | Immediate |

## D4 — Root cause (ranked; not concluded)

**What the data confirms:**
- **T1:** Insert T7-0031 cut parts across **4 lots** with no change logged.
- **T2:** Bore size climbed **26.0 µm** while it was in. It went up 10 measurements in a row, and the fit against time is strong (R² **0.876**). After the insert was replaced, the next part measured **22.007**, a drop of **−27.0 µm**.
- **Against:** there is only one measurement after the replacement.

| Rank | Candidate | Weak point |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (tie) | **C1:** the insert's cutting edge degraded (wear, chipping, or aluminium building up on the edge) | Nobody has confirmed the insert passed the 600-part limit; the data only proves at least 390 parts. Also, plain insert wear usually makes a bore smaller, not larger. |
| 1 (tie) | **C2:** the T7 offset or the boring-head setting drifted outward, and the insert change reset it | There's no offset record in the data to support or rule it out |
| 3 | C3: the coolant change from 6% to 8% sped up wear | No measurements from before the change, and size returned to normal with no coolant reversal |
| 4 | C4: shift, operator or heat | Shift and operator can't be separated (each shift had one operator). The growth carried straight through shift changes (+1.0, +1.0, +3.0 µm) and didn't drop back overnight. |
| 5 | C5: gauge error | In-process and final inspection gave the same readings |

**What would confirm or rule out each candidate:**
- **C1** is confirmed if the removed insert shows edge build-up, chipping or a changed shape, or if it cuts about 22.03 when refitted at the current offset. It is ruled out if the insert shows only normal wear, or cuts near nominal when refitted.
- **C2** is confirmed if the machine's offset history shows outward adjustments between 11-09 and 11-11, or the head setting changed at the insert change. It is ruled out if the offset never changed and the head wasn't touched.
- **C3** is confirmed if the new insert wears faster at 8% than past runs did at 6%. It is ruled out if the rates match.
- **C4** is confirmed if the new insert shows a rise during a shift or a drop overnight. It is ruled out if a run across a shift change shows no jump.
- **C5** is confirmed if the gauge fails a repeatability study or calibration check. It is ruled out if 5 held parts measure the same on a second calibrated gauge or CMM.

**Cheapest test to settle the tie:** pull the VMC-03 T7 offset history for 11-09 to 11-11 and look at insert T7-0031 under magnification. That separates C1 from C2. In the same pull, get the completed quantities for WO-8099, 8100 and 8101. They show whether the 600-part rule wasn't followed or was set at the wrong number. Until this runs, the tie stands.

**How it escaped:** the upward trend was visible in the measurements at **2026-11-10 07:20**, **7.83 h** before the first bad part, but nothing on the floor was set up to react to it.

**Why it was able to happen:** nothing enforced the 600-part insert limit from CAPA-071, and nobody ever checked whether that fix worked.

## D5 — Corrective actions

| # | Action | Breaks link |
|---|---|---|
| 5.1 | Insert life counter in the VMC-03 control that alarms and blocks cycle start at the limit, and resets only when an insert change is logged | T1: the insert can't stay in past its life (covers C1 and C2) |
| 5.2 | Set the insert life from measured data on the new insert (no more than 70% of the parts it takes to reach 22.015), replacing the unverified 600 | C1: "count exceeded the limit" |
| 5.3 | Control chart on Bore A, measured every 25th part. Six rising readings in a row, or any reading at 22.015 or above, means inspect or change the insert before the next part | T2: growth is caught before it reaches the limit (covers C1 and C2) |
| 5.4 | Lock the T7 offset (every change needs a recorded reason and is capped per shift), mark the head setting, and check it at every insert change. **Only if the test confirms C2.** | C2: "offset or head drifted" |
| 5.5 | Review the insert grade and edge preparation for this aluminium (6061), and coolant delivery to the bore. **Only if the test confirms C1.** | C1: "edge condition changed" |

The 25-part interval, the 22.015 guard band and the 70% factor are proposed settings, not calculated figures; the tooling engineer should confirm them. A gauge repeatability study is worth doing to support 5.3, but it's an improvement, not a corrective action, so it sits outside D5.

## D6 — Implement and verify *(blank placeholder)*
For each action: who implemented it, the date, how it was verified, the data, and who accepted it on what date.

## D7 — Prevent recurrence

| # | Why CAPA-071 failed | System change |
|---|---|---|
| 7.1 | The 600-part limit existed only on paper, and the insert ran through 4 lot changes | Insert life limits on tools cutting features with 25 µm or less of tolerance are enforced in the machine control. Setup sheets require a tool-life check at every work order or lot change. |
| 7.2 | CAPA-071 has been marked "not verified" since April and nothing flagged it | A corrective action can't close without a recorded effectiveness check. Any still unverified after 60 days goes on the monthly quality review. |
| 7.3 | NCR-0219's cause was accepted without examining the insert or checking the offsets, and plain wear doesn't explain oversize | **Reopen NCR-0219 and CAPA-071.** A bore-size root cause needs the offset history and a look at the tool before it is accepted. |
| 7.4 | A 21 µm bore had no in-process control | Every feature with 25 µm or less of total tolerance gets an in-process control chart with a reaction rule at release, across the whole part family |
| 7.5 | Parts shipped at 08:00, before the 10:05 finding | Shipping requires final-inspection sign-off on the lot |

**Effectiveness check (proposed):**

| Check | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| E1 | No Bore A over 22.021 across the next 3 VMC-03 lots, covering at least 2 counter-driven insert changes |
| E2 | Every control-chart signal has a logged reaction before the next part |
| E3 | Every insert change happens at or before the life limit, with no unrecorded override |
| E4 | Bore A Cpk is at least 1.33, calculated from the in-process data |
| E5 | NCR-0219 and CAPA-071 are dealt with under 7.3 |
| Customer | Northwind reports no further rejects in that period |

- **Proposed timing:** 30 days after 5.1–5.3 go in, or after the 3rd lot, whichever is later. The date isn't committed because implementation dates and the production schedule aren't on file.
- **If it fails:** reopen D4 rather than repeating the same action.
